measured_at: 2026-09-16 (local), main stack via make dev (search-svc 8801, ops-http 8803)
method: Candidate v47 (w_bm25=0.7) started as a 50% canary directly on search-svc POST /canary (background simulated ESCI replay). After >=30 canary requests, POST /debug/inject_latency {ms:250}. The ops-mcp guardrail watcher inside ops-http (poll interval 2 s, OPS_GUARDRAIL_INTERVAL default) detected the breach and called POST /models/rollback unattended. Timer polled GET /canary/status every 0.1 s: t0 = injection call returned, t1 = first status rolled_back. Registry, mlflow.db and ops.db were backed up before and restored after.

excluded_attempts.why_excluded: first script attempt; valid run but the script then hung (below) and was restarted, so the series was re-run from scratch
canary rolled back by the watcher before latency was injected (natural p95 188.9 ms > 150 ms and > 1.2x champion 126.2 ms on a busy CPU): a false-positive guardrail breach, no timing possible

caveats: Bounded by the 2 s watcher poll interval; times reflect where in the poll cycle the breach landed, n=3, no CI.
Simulated canary traffic inside search-svc on a laptop CPU; says nothing about production rollback time.
Canary was started on search-svc directly, not through the gated ops-mcp start_canary tool; only the rollback path is ops-mcp.
One unprovoked guardrail breach from CPU contention was seen in 5 attempts.
